newsitem.title: New Zealand: Pulp, paper stocks lead NZ shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Pulp, paper stocks lead NZ shares to higher close.

text.p: * New Zealand shares end with modest gain on higher volume
* Forest sector strengthens on renewed optimism
* Property for Industry, CIL actively traded
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +8.91 at 2,249.13
126 nil * NZSE-10 cap index +5.25 at 1,109.88
320 + 3 * NZSC cap index -11.15 at 4,924.95
309 + 3 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +4.64 at 1,850.40
341 - 1 * Volume NZ$60 million. Futures untraded
644 + 1 * Other movers - +5 -8
Pulp and paper stocks led the New Zealand share market to a modestly higher close on Tuesday on much-improved volume.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 8.91 points higher at 2,249.13 on turnover worth NZ$60 million.
"It was much better volume and the market had a more positive tone to it," Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch said.
Koller said it appeared the forest sector movement was on optimism that a recovery in pulp prices was in sight.
Fletcher Forests finished at NZ$1.95, Fletcher Paper at at $3.09 and Carter Holt Harvey at $3.20, all up three cents.
But the biggest trade of the day was in Property for Industry, with a line of 7.55 million shares trading for NZ$0.84 a share.
PFI, which last week reported a 33 percent increase in pre-tax first quarter earnings to NZ$2.12 million, ended the day up two cents to NZ$0.84.
Corporate Investments was also actively traded with 2.1 million shares crossing at NZ$0.70 a share, the stock later closing at a high for the year of NZ$0.71, up two.
Koller doubted there was anything new driving the stock, but noted CIL had been on the comeback trail for two years, the price appreciating by 200 percent in that time.
CIL owns Montana Wines and Truck Investments.

In mining, Summit Gold continued to take a hammering after an Australian analyst cast doubt on the commercial viability of its Valhalla, northern Queensland, uranium project. Summit finished eight cents down at NZ$0.30.
